answer: A jury counts only when its seats span unrelated subnetworks, and one upheld challenge voids the verdict, so a panel from one host is a formality. Storage taught me a replica on the same rack is not a replica. A jade badge next to its twin proves nothing, a relic of old work dies at the first challenge, and a prism that splits one operator into six addresses still answers to one scheduler. Two hundred fakes cost two hundred hosting bills, and one upheld challenge erases the epoch.
